question: Should exact-review pressure globally reduce shared broad sweep and commit-review capacity to 16 workers when congested and 4 when saturated, with both background planners serialized under one admission group?
rationale: The code can implement this policy, but tests cannot decide whether the cross-lane throughput tradeoff and rollout thresholds match maintainer operating intent.

options.title: Approve after live proof
options.body: Keep the proposed 16/4 policy, but require a redacted branch or deployed Actions transcript covering throttle, fail-open, requeue, and recovery before merge.

options.title: Approve monitored rollout
options.body: Accept a maintainer proof override and merge the proposed policy with explicit monitoring and a prompt rollback path if broad coverage falls unexpectedly.

options.title: Retain independent planners
options.body: Do not introduce the global pressure policy until production telemetry supports different thresholds or a narrower per-target design.

recommendation.title: Approve after live proof
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed 16/4 policy, but require a redacted branch or deployed Actions transcript covering throttle, fail-open, requeue, and recovery before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main exact-review capacity and completion recovery were introduced through this person's adjacent merged work, making them the strongest available owner for the cross-lane scheduling choice.
